acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Dragons family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Whelp, T1, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Hoard-Scent Ground Pouncer (Initiate) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two normal construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Wingless, with wet-looking juvenile scales, an oversized wedge-shaped head on a small deep-chested body, long tail, four claws, and nubs where the first horns will grow.

Signature mechanic: First Claim: the Whelp noses one loose hoard object into a visible circle and pounces at anything crossing the boundary; the oversized head pulls the landing forward, leaving the hornless nape and belly exposed until it scrambles around the claim again.
battlefieldDuty: Probe ground spacing by circling one claimed shiny object and making a committed four-legged pounce across its edge.
constructionDimensions: Anatomy and materials remain species-native and non-elemental: jewel- or metallic-tone scales, pale belly plates, horn, bone spur, leathery membranes, old scars, and physically fused hoard metal retain natural wear.

Motion and effects stay physical and bounded: claw gouges, wing-driven dust, membrane snap, shed scale, reflective eye-shine, and localized breath heat during exertion reveal force without persistent aura or magical trail.
counterplay: Feint across one side of the circle and leave before launch, then cross behind the rigid tail and strike the exposed nape or pale belly during the clumsy landing. Affinity signal: Wing knuckles, horn pivots, pale belly seams, breath cadence, hoard anchors, and marked takeoff or landing lanes preserve each form's established weak point.
forbiddenTreatments: Affinity-neutral spectacle that hides the Dragon's age, wings, horns, or territorial equipment
identityInvariants: Long neck and tail, deep chest, four clawed limbs, wedge-shaped horned skull, and wings that emerge and expand after the wingless first form.
Each individual holds one coherent metallic or jewel-tone scale identity with a paler underbelly and bright reflective eyes, rather than changing base identity by affinity.
Overlapping scales, horn, bone spurs, and leathery wing membrane retain reptilian load paths and readable joints at every tier.
Horn crowns, spinal ridges, battle scars, torn membrane, and hoard metal fused into old belly scales accumulate as age and territorial history.
Wingspan and horn crown escalate together from absent wings and horn nubs to storm-front wings and branching imperial antlers, while the ground-to-sky grammar remains recognizable.
telegraph: Wet-looking scales tighten over the hind legs, the oversized head lowers beside the shiny claim, and the long tail goes rigid along the intended pounce line.
